Same as message decorations, except they appear next to members in the member list.

Define the `renderMemberListDecorator` method on your plugin object to make use of this feature.

# Native NodeJS Code

> How to run code in NodeJS

Plugins run in the browser sandbox by default. This means they only have access to web APIs as if they were running in a regular web browser.

Sometimes plugins may need access to the NodeJS environment. Some examples include

* Bypassing Content Security Policy (CSP) or Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) restrictions
* Interfacing with other programs
* Reading specific files from the filesystem

However, this **should only be used as a last resort** if no other alternatives are available! For example, the following are not valid use cases:

* Storing data — Instead, use Limey V1 Settings or IndexedDB (via DataStore API)
* Reading or writing arbitrary files — This poses severe security risks. Use web file picker/saving instead

## Defining Native Plugin Code

[Section titled “Defining Native Plugin Code”](#defining-native-plugin-code)

Plugin Natives are defined via the `native.ts` file in your plugin folder. This file will be ran in the NodeJS environment. This file can export functions to make them available via IPC.

Any function exported from here

* will be callable via Limey V1Native as demonstrated below
* will always return a Promise
* will receive the invoke event as first argument. You do not pass this event from the browser code.

- native.ts

  ```ts
  export function add(event: IpcMainInvokeEvent, x: number, y: number) {
      return x + y;
  }
  ```

- index.ts(x)

  ```js
  import definePlugin, { PluginNative } from "@utils/types";


  const Native = Limey V1Native.pluginHelpers.MyPluginName as PluginNative<typeof import("./native")>;


  export default definePlugin({
      name: "MyPluginName",
      async start() {
          console.log(await Native.add(1, 2)); // logs 3
      }
  })
  ```

Danger

You should consider the browser process untrusted. Any data passed as arguments must be carefully validated and sanitized.

Do not export overly broad APIs. Only export minimal, necessary functions. For example, if you need to read one specific file on the host, hardcode that specific file path **inside your native code** rather than accepting it as an argument from the browser.

If you are accepting an argument and including it in a file path or a shell command, you must carefully validate and sanitize it to prevent security vulnerabilities like path traversal or command injection.

Caution

After making changes to the native.ts file, you will need to fully close and restart Discord for the changes to take effect.

DO NOT import the `native.ts` file directly into your browser code, as this will cause errors! You can only access it via Limey V1Native global!

Any value you pass as argument and return value must be [serializable via the structured clone algorithm](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Web_Workers_API/Structured_clone_algorithm#supported_types).

## Bypassing Content Security Policy (CSP) and Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS)

[Section titled “Bypassing Content Security Policy (CSP) and Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS)”](#bypassing-content-security-policy-csp-and-cross-origin-resource-sharing-cors)

[CSP](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Guides/CSP) and [CORS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/CORS) are web security mechanisms that restrict which resources can be loaded and from which websites.

They are pretty similar with one key difference:

* **CSP** is set by the current website and enforced by the Browser. Discord tells the Browser “only allow resources from discord.com, tenor.com, …”. Then if code tries to load `example.com`, the browser blocks it
* **CORS** is set by the server hosting the resource and enforced by the Browser. The server at `example.com` says “only allow example.com to access my resources”. Then the browser blocks discord.com from requesting it.

In other words, CSP is controlled by us, while CORS is controlled by the server hosting the resource.

### CSP

[Section titled “CSP”](#csp)

To bypass CSP, just add the target server to the CspPolicies in your native.ts file:

* native.ts

  ```ts
  import { ConnectSrc, CspPolicies } from "@main/csp";


  CspPolicies["example.com"] = ConnectSrc; // or MediaSrc, etc
  ```

* index.ts(x)

  ```ts
  const res = await fetch("https://example.com/endpoint"); // now allowed
  ```

### CORS

[Section titled “CORS”](#cors)

CORS however cannot be modified by us, as the Server controls it. Instead, you must send the request from your native code, as NodeJS does not enforce CORS:

* native.ts

  ```ts
  const API_HOST = "https://example.com";


  export async function fetchCoolAPI(_event, endpoint: string) {
      // endpoint argument is untrusted! Validate it before using it.
      const url = new URL(endpoint, API_HOST);
      if (url.origin !== API_HOST) {
          throw new Error("Invalid endpoint");
      }


      const res = await fetch(url.toString());
      return await res.json();
  }
  ```

* index.ts(x)

  ```ts
  import definePlugin, { PluginNative } from "@utils/types";


  const Native = Limey V1Native.pluginHelpers.MyPluginName as PluginNative<typeof import("./native")>;


  export default definePlugin({
      name: "MyPluginName",
      async start() {
          console.log(await Native.fetchCoolAPI("/some-endpoint")); // logs the JSON response from https://example.com/some-endpoint
      }
  })
  ```

Danger

Don’t export an overly broad fetch API from your native code as this completely undermines the security model and can expose sensitive data. Always restrict it to specific endpoints or domains.

In the above example, the fetch API is restricted to the `https://example.com` domain, ensuring that only requests to this specific server are allowed.

# Patches

> Patch Discord's code to modify its behavior

Note

You may not need a patch. Limey V1 offers many [built-in APIs](/plugins/common) for modifying Discord’s behavior without needing to write a patch.

Patches are [RegExp](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/RegExp) replacements applied to Discord’s JavaScript code at runtime. They allow you to rewrite Discord’s code in any way you want. For example, you can remove undesired code or checks, insert your own code, replace code with alternative implementations, etc.

If you don’t know RegExp, you should first learn it before attempting to write patches.

***

Before writing a patch, you must understand [how modules work](/discord-code/modules).

Writing a patch is a three step process:

1. Find the part of Discord’s code you want to modify. See [Finding Code](/discord-code/find-code).
2. Come up with the patch [**`find`**](#the-find) — a unique string contained in the module you want to patch
3. Write a RegExp [**match**](#the-match) and [**replace**](#the-replace)

Caution

DevTools will pretty-print code and add extra whitespace. However, Discord’s code is minified and will **never** contain unnecessary whitespace. When writing a find or match, do not include whitespace.

## The `find`

[Section titled “The find”](#the-find)

I will assume that you found the module you want to patch.

The next step is to identify a unique sequence of code that is contained **only** in the module you want to patch. Avoid using minified variable names, as they may change between Discord updates.

The best suited anchors for finds are

* Intl strings like `S.intl.formatToPlainString(S.t["a9+V+V"]` — The ID `a9+V+V"` is stable and can be used. `S` is unstable and should not be used
* Function/Method names — Non mangled names are a great choice
* Unique strings — Any string that is unlikely to appear elsewhere in Discord’s code

Combine that with surrounding code like `:`, `(`, `{`, etc., to make it more unique and less likely to appear elsewhere in Discord’s code.

Some example finds from existing plugins:

* `}renderStickersAccessories(` — A method defined inside our module
* `.CREATE_FORUM_POST||` — A non-mangled property in our Module
* `#{intl::PREMIUM_MESSAGE_LENGTH_UPSELL_TOOLTIP}` — An Intl message by non-hashed name. See [Intl Keys](#intl-keys) for more details.
* `#{intl::a9+V+V::raw}` — An Intl message by hashed name. See [Intl Keys](#intl-keys) for more details. ( Once you picked a find, use global source search `CTRL + SHIFT + F`) to search for this find and ensure it’s only found in exactly one module.

## The `match`

[Section titled “The match”](#the-match)

This is a RegExp which will operate on the module found by your `find`. Supports the following custom syntax:

* `#{intl::KEY}` for non-hashed keys, see [Intl Keys](#intl-keys)
* `#{intl::HASH::raw}` for hashed keys
* `\i` to match minified javascript identifiers (names of variables, functions, etc)

For example, to match

```js
t.type !== g.lp.ACTIVITY && _.A.selectParticipant(c, t.id);
```

you could use the following `match`:

```js
\i\.type!==\i\.\i\.ACTIVITY&&\i\.\i\.selectParticipant\(\i,\i\.id\)
```

If you want to refer to minified variables in your replacement, capture them using [capturing groups](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Guide/Regular_Expressions/Groups_and_Ranges).

For example, to capture the participant ID (`t.id`), you could use the following `match` — note the extra parentheses around it:

```js
\i\.type!==\i\.\i\.ACTIVITY&&\i\.\i\.selectParticipant\(\i,(\i\.id)\)
```

## The `replace`

[Section titled “The replace”](#the-replace)

This is the replacement string. Any code captured in the `match` **will be replaced** with this value.

You can use many special identifiers here:

* `$&` to refer to the entire RegExp match
* `$1`, `$2`, etc. to refer to captured groups in the `match`
* `$$` to refer to a literal `$` character
* `$self` to insert your plugin instance. This allows you to call methods defined on your plugin.

## Using plugin methods inside patches

[Section titled “Using plugin methods inside patches”](#using-plugin-methods-inside-patches)

Replacement strings should be as short as possible. Writing code in them is very prone to errors since it’s not validated by your Editor.

Instead, define a method on your plugin and call it from the replacement string using `$self.methodName()`.

### Example

[Section titled “Example”](#example)

You can call methods and render components from your plugin within the replacement strings.

Components must always be wrapped in an error boundary to prevent crashes. If there is any chance that a method might throw an error, it should use a `try...catch` block to handle errors gracefully. This is always the case if you use Webpack modules, as they could break or change shape.

```jsx
definePlugin({
    // ...


    patches: [
        {
            find: "...",
            replacement: [
                {
                    match: /.../,
                    replace: "$self.doThing($1)"
                },
                {
                    match: /.../,
                    replace: "$self.renderComponent({ text: $1 })"
                }
            ]
        }
    ],


    doThing(arg) {
        try {
            console.log(arg);
        } catch (e) {
            logger.error(e);
        }
    },


    renderComponent: ErrorBoundary.wrap(props => <div>{props.text}</div>)
});
```

## Patch Safety

[Section titled “Patch Safety”](#patch-safety)

It is always better for your patch to break after a change than to match the wrong code and potentially cause crashes.

To achieve this, make sure that your patch is specific. Always try to anchor it on a non-mangled identifier to avoid unintended replacements. Use wildcards sparingly to minimize the risk of accidental matches.

### Unsafe example

[Section titled “Unsafe example”](#unsafe-example)

This is an unsafe match because it is a very generic match. This could easily match unintended code and cause issues.

```regexp
ref:(\i),style:\i
```

### Safe example

[Section titled “Safe example”](#safe-example)

This still matches the same code, but we now anchor it to a specific context via a [lookahead](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Regular_expressions/Lookahead_assertion) for the relevant Intl key. The match is only accepted if the specified Intl key appears within the next 250 characters.

```js
ref:(\i),style:\i(?=.{0,250}#{intl::USER_PROFILE_ACCOUNT_POPOUT_BUTTON_A11Y_LABEL})
```

## Patch Performance

[Section titled “Patch Performance”](#patch-performance)

Some Discord modules are **huge**, and an inefficient Regular Expression can significantly impact performance. Debug builds of Limey V1 will log how long your patch took to the console.

TODO - add guide

## Intl Keys

[Section titled “Intl Keys”](#intl-keys)

User facing messages are stored as Intl messages. Each such message has a unique identifier:

* In Discord’s source code, these identifiers have human-readable names like `PREMIUM_MESSAGE_LENGTH_UPSELL_TOOLTIP`.
* In the minified code we are working with, these identifiers are instead replaced with hashed names like `a9+V+V`. These names are stable so you can use them in finds and matches. You can search for these keys via global source search (`CTRL + SHIFT + F`) to see what message they correspond to.

We have a huge list of mappings which you can use to find human-readable names for a hash. You can download it from <https://sadan.zip/assets/key-mappings.json>.

If there is no mapping for your hash, you can try to guess it based on the context if you want, but this is completely optional. You can hash an identifier using `Limey V1.Util.runtimeHashMessageKey("KEYBIND_IN_BROSWER_NOTICE")` in the DevTools console.

Intl messages are referenced in finds or matches using special syntax:

* `#{intl::KEY}` for non-hashed keys
* `#{intl::HASH::raw}` for hashed keys

You can combine these with surrounding code, e.g. `#{intl::GUILD_OWNER}),children:`

# Plugin Submission

> How to submit your plugin to the official Limey V1 repository



# Release Channels

> Complete specification of release channels, build types, rollout strategies and maintenance states for Limey V1 — official vs. proposed

This page is the specification for a **release manager / updater / launcher / settings menu** for Limey V1 (a Vencord fork). It catalogues every channel name in the release-management space — which ones actually exist in the codebase, which ones are Discord’s own client branches, and which ones are *proposed custom labels* you can adopt without pretending upstream ships them.

🏷 Origin tiers

Each entry is tagged **Official · Limey**, **Official · upstream Vencord**, **Discord client**, **Discord rollout process**, or **Proposed**. Nothing is claimed official unless the code shows it.

📐 Three axes

Names only become useful when split into three orthogonal axes: *Track* (what code), *Host* (which Discord build), *Rollout* (how it reaches users). See the [recommended hierarchy](#recommended-hierarchy).

🔤 Naming

IDs are lowercase kebab-case (`stable`, `dev`, `canary-rollout`), suited for config keys, CLI flags and update feeds. Display names are Title Case for UI menus.

## Accuracy notes (read first)

[Section titled “Accuracy notes (read first)”](#accuracy-notes-read-first)

* **What Limey V1 officially ships today.** Two build tracks: the **Stable** builds served by the installer from the Limey backend, and **DevBuilds** built from source (self-identified, git-based updater active). Both target the desktop Discord app; a **Web** flavor ships as browser extension / userscript / browser bundle.
* **What upstream Vencord officially ships.** The same two-track model (Stable + Development/DevBuild) with web/user builds — Limey V1 inherits it.
* **What Discord ships.** Four official client branches: **Stable**, **PTB**, **Canary**, **Development** (all four are detected by the installer on Linux). Discord additionally runs its own *rollout processes* (canary rollout, staged/progressive numlock rollouts) — those are processes, not user-selectable channels.
* **Everything else** — Preview, Beta, Alpha, RC, Nightly, Snapshot, Edge, Insider, Early Access, LTS, Legacy, hotfix pipelines, blue-green, shadow releases, feature-flagged and A/B testing — is a **proposed custom label** borrowed from industry practice (GitHub, Chrome, Firefox, Kubernetes, and so on). Adopt them freely; just don’t advertise them as built-in.

## Where this spec is implemented

[Section titled “Where this spec is implemented”](#where-this-spec-is-implemented)

The registry is not just prose — the platform now serves and renders it:

| Integration               | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `GET /v1/channels`        | Schema-versioned manifest (`limey.v1/channels/1`) of every channel above, each entry carrying `origin`, `stability`, `cadence` and an `implemented` flag. Single-channel lookup at `/v1/channels/:id`. |
| Bot SDK `client.channels` | `list()`, `get(id)` and `manifest()` for bots that want to report or validate channels.                                                                                                                |
| Updater settings section  | The desktop settings **Updater** tab shows the active track (`stable` or `dev` via the standalone-build rule) and names the planned channels explicitly as not shipping yet.                           |
| Updater runtime           | Builds are tagged at compile time: `--standalone` → `stable`, source builds → `dev` (DevBuild self-identification, git updater).                                                                       |

Proposed channels stay definition-only everywhere: no artifact paths, feed URLs or branches exist for them, here or in the API.

## Stability scale

[Section titled “Stability scale”](#stability-scale)

All rows below use this five-level scale:

| Level      | Meaning                                                               |
| ---------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Production | Fit for default use by anyone; releases are deliberate and reviewable |
| Testing    | Reasonably safe; expect occasional rough edges                        |
| Unstable   | Minutes-to-hours freshness; breakage is expected, not exceptional     |
| Volatile   | Arbitrary machine state; no support contract                          |
| Internal   | Diagnostic-only; never distribute                                     |

## Legend for the “Origin” column

[Section titled “Legend for the “Origin” column”](#legend-for-the-origin-column)

| Tag                 | Meaning                                                              |
| ------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Limey**           | Official Limey V1 build channel (currently served / installable)     |
| **Vencord**         | Inherited official concept from upstream Vencord                     |
| **Discord**         | Official Discord client release channel                              |
| **Discord·process** | Discord’s rollout mechanism in production — not a selectable channel |
| **Proposed**        | Suggested custom label for this spec; not implemented anywhere       |

***

## 1. Main release channels

[Section titled “1. Main release channels”](#1-main-release-channels)

Sorted most stable → most experimental.

| ID        | Display Name            | Origin                                                                                                                                                | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | Intended audience                                | Stability                  | Update frequency                      | Recommended use case                                                 |
| --------- | ----------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------- | ------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `stable`  | Stable                  | **Limey / Vencord / Discord**                                                                                                                         | The default, reviewed track. Installer pulls hash-stamped builds from the Limey backend; changelog is cut per release.                                                                                                      | Everyone                                         | Production                 | Deliberate (per feature batch or fix) | Daily use; the only track recommended to non-developers              |
| `lts`     | Stable LTS              | **Proposed** (concept: enterprise LTS)                                                                                                                | A frozen snapshot of `stable` supported for a long window, accepting only security and crash fixes.                                                                                                                         | Hosters, admins, people who hate change          | Production                 | Rarely → never                        | Downtime-sensitive setups, fork packagers                            |
| `rc`      | Release Candidate       | **Proposed**                                                                                                                                          | The final pre-release of the next stable version; feature-complete, only crash/security fixes allowed. Folded into `stable` once clean.                                                                                     | Testers and plugin authors pre-validating        | Testing                    | One per release cycle                 | Verify “breaking” changes before they reach everyone                 |
| `beta`    | Beta                    | **Proposed** (concept: upstream Vencord *plugin-level* beta exists via plugin `beta` field, but not as a client channel)                              | Public pre-release track accumulating features for the next version; wider audience than RC, less polish.                                                                                                                   | Curious users who accept some breakage           | Testing                    | Per feature batch                     | Trying features early without maintenance-every-day cost             |
| `ptb`     | Public Test Build (PTB) | **Discord**                                                                                                                                           | Discord’s own public-testing client branch. Limey V1 installs into it (installer detects `DiscordPTB`), but PTB itself is Discord’s release cadence, not a Limey channel.                                                   | Discord testers                                  | Testing (Discord’s choice) | Discord-driven, weekly-ish            | Reproducing Discord-platform bugs; early Discord features            |
| `preview` | Preview                 | **Proposed**                                                                                                                                          | Neutral umbrella “pre-stable” name for people who want newer-than-stable but not bleeding-edge. Can simply alias `beta` or `rc`.                                                                                            | Non-technical early adopters                     | Testing                    | With each dev batch                   | A friendly label for an “opt into newer stuff” toggle in settings UI |
| `canary`  | Canary                  | **Discord** (Discord client) / **Proposed** for Limey V1 itself (client mods usually ship stable-only; upstream Vencord does not cut client canaries) | Note the crucial ambiguity: **Canary branch** = latest, usually-next-day Discord client provided by Discord; **Canary rollout** = gradual delivery. This spec reserves the name for the Discord client *branch* by default. | Discord-adjacent testers                         | Unstable (Discord side)    | Daily, from Discord                   | Catching changes in Discord’s code that affect Limey V1 patches      |
| `alpha`   | Alpha                   | **Proposed**                                                                                                                                          | Code that will change shape; no freeze promise.                                                                                                                                                                             | Plugin developers porting against the future API | Unstable                   | per commit or per batch               | Porting plugins to upcoming internal API changes                     |

**Overlap notes.** `beta`/`rc`/`preview` describe *stages* of the same flow (feature-batch → polish → freeze). Keep all three only if you want a public changelog narrative; otherwise collapse to `preview`.

***

## 2. Development channels

[Section titled “2. Development channels”](#2-development-channels)

Sorted most usable → most volatile.

| ID                                 | Display Name        | Origin                                         | Description                                                                                                                                                                  | Intended audience                        | Stability | Update frequency                            | Recommended use case                                                |
| ---------------------------------- | ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- | --------- | ------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `dev`                              | Development         | **Limey / Vencord** (official; the “DevBuild”) | Source-built flavor of Limey V1. Self-identifies as a DevBuild (support warning + git updater active) instead of silently pretending to be a release.                        | Developers, contributors, power users    | Unstable  | Per commit; git updater pulls from the repo | Debugging, contributing, running new plugins before they’re blessed |
| `devbuild`                         | DevBuild            | **Limey / Vencord** (official alias)           | The *runtime label* of a `dev` build. Use as an alias in the updater so “Am I on devbuild?” logic has one canonical id.                                                      | (same as `dev`)                          | Unstable  | = `dev`                                     | Same as `dev`; keep as alias, not separate channel                  |
| `source`                           | Source Build        | **Limey / Vencord** (officially supported)     | Any install built by the user from their own checkout (e.g. the local dev scripts). Includes locally modified code; updater operates against git by definition.              | Developers                               | Volatile  | On next manual build                        | Verifying fixes before contributing; hot-patching upstream          |
| `custom`                           | Custom Build        | **Proposed** (extends the above)               | A user-built flavor from a fork with extra patches, distinct branding or plugin changes. Needs a `channel-owner` field so the updater knows who’s authoritative.             | Fork maintainers                         | Volatile  | Owner-driven                                | Community forks, personal modpacks of plugins                       |
| `nightly`                          | Nightly             | **Proposed** (Firefox-model name)              | Scheduled (e.g. 00:00 UTC) snapshot of the main branch, built automatically even if commits are broken.                                                                      | Continuous-testers & plugin CI           | Unstable  | Daily                                       | Automated cross-testing; making “I update once a day” a promise     |
| `snapshot`                         | Snapshot            | **Proposed**                                   | Point-in-time named dev build (like Gradle/JVM snapshots). Differentiator vs nightly: snapshot inclusion is *manual* or gated by tests, nightly is a cron.                   | Same as nightly                          | Unstable  | Irregular                                   | Publishing “here’s a build with the fix to test” quickly            |
| `edge`                             | Edge                | **Proposed** (Heroku/Vercel-model name)        | Purest freshness: same-source as `nightly` but built per successful push, no schedule.                                                                                       | CI systems, ultra-impatient contributors | Volatile  | Per push                                    | Smoke-testing the exact commit that just landed                     |
| `experimental`                     | Experimental        | **Proposed**                                   | Aggregates exceptional, opt-in functionality(feature-flagged plugins, rewrites) pinned to a stable-ish base.                                                                 |                                          |           |                                             |                                                                     |
| Plugin authors & opt-in flag flips | Unstable / Volatile | With the experiments                           | Testing one specific feature without taking all dev-build risk                                                                                                               |                                          |           |                                             |                                                                     |
| `debug`                            | Debug               | **Proposed**                                   | Builds with verbose logging, sourcemaps, devtools unwrapping, integrity checks off — never meant to leave a machine. Support for reports: “please attach a debug-build log”. | Core developers                          | Internal  | On demand                                   | Diagnosing silent failures in `stable` or `dev`                     |

**Overlap notes.** `nightly` vs `snapshot` vs `edge` differ only in *what triggers a build* (cron / test-gate / push). Ship one of them; pick `nightly` if you want a Firefox-style cadence, `edge` if you want maximum freshness. `dev` vs `devbuild`: keep `dev` as the channel id and `devbuild` as its display/runtime alias so existing error-report wording keeps working.

***

## 3. Early access channels

[Section titled “3. Early access channels”](#3-early-access-channels)

All of these are **Proposed** — none exist anywhere upstream. They exist to give marketing-friendly names to subsets of the technical channels above.

| ID            | Display Name      | Origin                                   | Description                                                                                                                                          | Intended audience                                                | Stability            | Update frequency              | Recommended use case                                            |
| ------------- | ----------------- | ---------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------- | ----------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `early`       | Early Access      | **Proposed**                             | Paid/logged-in users get the next feature batch a little earlier, still built from `rc`-quality code.                                                | Limes perk-tier subscribers (optional perk on the economy tiers) | Testing              | Same as `beta`/`rc`           | An “offline-friendly opt-in” in the settings menu               |
| `insider`     | Insider           | **Proposed** (Windows/Chrome-model name) | A “read the dev diary” crowd — same artifacts as `beta` but with release notes aggregated per batch rather than per channel.                         | People who want to know *why* changes are happening              | Testing              | Batch-shaped                  | Same artifact as `beta`; choose purely for naming/UX preference |
| `preview-ch`  | Preview Channel   | **Proposed** (Android/model name)        | Just a friendlier display name for `beta`. Kept here so the settings menu can say “Preview (Beta)” without looking jargonny.                         | Same as `beta`                                                   | Testing              | Same as `beta`                | Pure naming-fallback; another name users search for             |
| `dev-preview` | Developer Preview | **Proposed**                             | Guaranteed spec-stable-ish subset of the upcoming release — the ones *plugin authors* depend on (API changes, plugin manifest schema, patch points). | Plugin ecosystem maintainers                                     | Testing (API-frozen) | Per planned release milestone | Migrating to the next plugin API before it ships                |
| `internal`    | Internal Testing  | **Proposed**                             | Small ring for core collaborators before anything public: internal checksums, unreleased ban-heuristic tuning, security-sensitive fixes.             | Core team                                                        | Testing or worse     | Irregular                     | Round-0 verification of an upcoming security patch              |
| `community`   | Community Preview | **Proposed**                             | Public “vote on what’s next” lobe where the top-voted candidate experiments advance to `beta`.                                                       | Plugin community, store authors                                  | Testing              | Community-driven              | Democratic direction-setting, not just bug-catch                |

**Overlap notes.** `early` / `insider` / `preview-ch` are *branding names* for more or less the same artifact as `beta` — pick one word for your UI and define the rest as aliases in the release-manager data model rather than shipping three independent channels.

***

## 4. Deployment / rollout strategies

[Section titled “4. Deployment / rollout strategies”](#4-deployment--rollout-strategies)

These are **Discord·process** (where they exist at Discord) or **Proposed/proven industry patterns** — *strategies*, not user-selectable channels. A release manager should pair each with one or more *tracks* from the tables above.

| ID               | Display Name                         | Origin                                                                                    | Description                                                                                           | Intended audience                                   | Stability                 | Update frequency                 | Recommended use case                                                                                                 |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------- | -------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `full`           | Immediate / Full rollout             | Concept everywhere, effectively what Limey V1 does today                                  | Newest build is served to everyone as soon as its hash changes.                                       | Everyone                                            | Production                | Per release                      | The default, matches current **Stable**                                                                              |
| `canary-rollout` | Canary Rollout                       | **Discord·process** / **Proposed** for Limey V1                                           | Ship first to a tiny percentage of volunteers (often `dev`-track users) before the broader audience.  | Volunteers                                          | Production (early cohort) | Per release, percentage-driven   | Catch client-specific regressions with minimal blast radius                                                          |
| `progressive`    | Progressive Rollout (Staged rollout) | **Discord·process** (numlock-based % cohorts are in Discord’s own updater) / **Proposed** | Percentage cohorts (1% → 10% → 50% → 100%), each gated on error telemetry.                            | Everyone, spread over time                          | Production                | Per release window               | Universal, boring, extremely effective default                                                                       |
| `phased`         | Phased Rollout                       | **Proposed** (same family, cohort-by-cohort on a calendar rather than telemetry)          | Fixed dates for steps (“2026-10-25: 10%”) rather than percentage health gates.                        | Ops/forks with uptime contracts                     | Production                | Planned windows                  | Coordinating across maintainers, companies or server regions                                                         |
| `rolling`        | Rolling Release                      | **Proposed** (apt/arch/Rust toolchain model name)                                         | No versioned releases at all — updates continuously.                                                  | Developers & tinkerers                              | Unstable                  | Continuous                       | Exactly what `dev` already is; use this term when explaining the model, not as a channel                             |
| `bluegreen`      | Blue-Green Deployment                | **Proposed** (deployment topology, not a channel)                                         | Run current build (blue) and new build (green) simultaneously; switch the pointer after health-check. | Backend / server.js wearing hats                    | Production                | Per deploy                       | Zero-downtime backend deploys for the Limey V1 API itself                                                            |
| `shadow`         | Shadow Release                       | **Proposed**                                                                              | New code runs, takes traffic, produces logs/metrics, but its user-visible output is discarded.        | Performance & safety instrumentation                | Internal                  | Per experiment                   | Measuring a rewritten patching routine against identical Discord traffic                                             |
| `featureflagged` | Feature-Flagged Release              | **Proposed** (well-established industry pattern)                                          | Ship a binary to `stable` containing *disabled* features, then enable them per-user remotely.         | Everyone (features are opt-in, code path is shared) | Production                | Continuous, no re-install needed | Frequent-Safe experimentation without new builds; pairs perfectly with Limey’s Limes/perk tiers to gate early access |
| `abtest`         | A/B Testing                          | **Proposed** (established industry pattern)                                               | Two variants of the same feature delivered to random cohorts, decision made on measured outcomes.     | Data-driven UI/UX work                              | Production (per-cohort)   | Per experiment                   | Reflowing plugin-store pages or settings-menu UX with real data                                                      |

**Overlap notes.** `canary-rollout` ⊂ `progressive` ⊂ `phased` — the same family at different calibration styles (volunteer / telemetry / calendar). Pick exactly one as the Limey V1 production strategy; keep the others in the release-manager schema as synonyms for different sensitivities.

***

## 5. Maintenance and support channels

[Section titled “5. Maintenance and support channels”](#5-maintenance-and-support-channels)

States and processes a track can enter — not (usually) channels users choose.

| ID               | Display Name        | Origin                                                                                     | Description                                                                                                                                                     | Intended audience                            | Stability            | Update frequency                                | Recommended use case                                                   |
| ---------------- | ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- | -------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `lts`            | Stable LTS          | **Proposed**                                                                               | See §1. A *state* `stable` may enter: a release line is declared LTS and stops taking features.                                                                 | Long-cycle operators, maintainers, packagers | Production           | Security/crash-fixes only for the frozen window | Long-supported install baselines                                       |
| `maintenance`    | Maintenance Release | **Proposed**                                                                               | Bug-fix-only drop on an otherwise-frozen track.                                                                                                                 | Users of a given version                     | Production           | As bugs are fixed                               | Polish between feature batches                                         |
| `hotfix`         | Hotfix              | **Proposed** (standard industry idiom)                                                     | Out-of-band patch applied bypassing normal gates because the live product is broken.                                                                            | Everyone (fast-tracked)                      | Production (usually) | As needed                                       | Fixing a broken build or a widespread plugin outage right now          |
| `security-patch` | Security Patch      | **Proposed** (concept known industry-wide; upstream Vencord itself does push urgent fixes) | Same as hotfix, plus *silent deploy priority* — security-sensitive fixes should reach `stable` before a changelog is cut.                                       | Everyone                                     | Production           | As vulnerabilities are found                    | Patching patchers or anti-scam/anti-scam heuristics                    |
| `rollback`       | Rollback            | **Proposed** (operations concept)                                                          | Re-point users to the previous hash after a bad release. Keeps a “last known good” pointer in the backend to enable one-click revert.                           | Users being protected                        | Production           | Emergency only                                  | Recovering from a bad `stable` push without waiting for the next patch |
| `legacy`         | Legacy              | **Proposed**                                                                               | Old client-version-limited builds kept around for users who cannot (or will not) update their Discord client. Tool must state concrete “supported until” dates. | Users on old Discord versions                | Testing (frozen)     | Patch-stratified, rare                          | Long-tail Discord-version support                                      |
| `deprecated`     | Deprecated          | **Proposed** (real concept upstream for *plugins*, proposed here for *tracks*)             | A channel scheduled to be removed; updater should nag with a transition link.                                                                                   | Everyone                                     | Any                  | Until removal                                   | Cleaning up rarely-loaded channels without surprise delivery           |
| `archived`       | Archived            | **Proposed**                                                                               | Read-only snapshots of any channel, no binaries served, no support. Users cannot “install” it; they can only *inspect* old artifacts.                           | Historians, forensics                        | Frozen               | Never updates                                   | Audit trail, crash-regression archaeology                              |

**Overlap notes.** `hotfix` / `security-patch` / `maintenance` are the same mechanism at different urgencies (breakage → fix, vulnerability → fix, minor bug → fix). Keep IDs distinct in the schema so a release manager can attach different deploy gating to each, even though they reuse the same artifact pipeline. `legacy`/`archived`/`deprecated`/`lts` are all *states a track can be in*, with distinct user promises (old-but-hot / read-only / dying / long-supported).

***

## 6. Discord client compatibility (install targets)

[Section titled “6. Discord client compatibility (install targets)”](#6-discord-client-compatibility-install-targets)

These are **Discord**’s own client branches plus *where* Limey V1 actually runs. The installer already detects and supports all four desktop branches, and the web bundle runs in browsers. Keep these as a *second axis* in your release manager (`host`), never as a replacement for the first (`track`).

| ID                    | Display Name                         | Origin              | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                | Intended audience                              | Stability                                        | Update frequency                | Recommended use case                                  |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------------ | ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `discord-stable`      | Discord Stable                       | **Discord**         | The mainstream Discord desktop app everyone has.                                                                                                                                                           | Everyone                                       | Production (Discord’s)                           | Weekly-ish, Discord-driven      | Default install target                                |
| `discord-ptb`         | Public Test Build (Discord PTB)      | **Discord**         | Discord’s wide pre-stable branch, available on the Download page.                                                                                                                                          | Opt-in testers                                 | Testing (Discord’s)                              | Weekly-ish, before wide release | Bug replication; early CSS/DOM drift                  |
| `discord-canary`      | Discord Canary                       | **Discord**         | Discord’s fastest-moving client, near-day freshness.                                                                                                                                                       | Discord-adjacent testers                       | Unstable (Discord’s)                             | Near daily                      | Catching patch targets the moment they drift          |
| `discord-development` | Development (Discord Development)    | **Discord**         | Discord’s internal-flavor branch occasionally distributed for testers.                                                                                                                                     | Discord staff & client mod devs                | Volatile (Discord’s)                             | Erratic                         | Verifying patches against unreleased internal BFS     |
| `desktop`             | Desktop Client (patched Discord app) | **Limey / Vencord** | Limey V1’s format: injected `patcher.js`/`preload.js`/`renderer.js`/`renderer.css` installed into one of the four Discord branches above by the installer.                                                 | Desktop users                                  | Depends on the *track* chosen                    | Per station’s track             | The main product on the desktop                       |
| `web`                 | Web Client (browser)                 | **Limey / Vencord** | Limey V1’s browser bundle — Chrome MV3 extension, Firefox MV2 shell, userscripts for discord.com.                                                                                                          | Browser-first users (incl. mobile Discord web) | Matches `stable` (web usually ships stable-only) | Per stable release              | Users who can’t or won’t run an injector/UI installer |
| `custom-client`       | Custom Client Build                  | **Proposed**        | Any other Discord-compatible client (VDI, EmbeddedApp builds, Electron-based forks shipped by other projects). Disclaimer required: compatibility is not guaranteed, plugin authors can’t test against it. | Fork operators                                 | Volatile                                         | Owner-driven                    | Power users in restricted environments                |

**Overlap notes.** `discord-canary` (a Discord *client branch*) is often confused with “Limey V1 canary” (a *track* of Limey V1 code). In a release manager they should be two different fields — e.g. `track: canary-rollout` plus `host: discord-canary` — even though the installer just reads the code for whatever Discord branch it sits inside.

***

## Recommended hierarchy

[Section titled “Recommended hierarchy”](#recommended-hierarchy)

The mistake most release systems make is treating all of the above as one flat list. Limey V1 has three genuinely different things, and keeping them separate keeps the settings menu honest:

```plaintext
release-manager
├── TRACK        which Limey V1 code you run          (choose 1)
│   ├── stable      → default, installer-served, changelogged ✅  TODAY
│   ├── dev         → DevBuild, git-updater, support warning  ✅  TODAY
│   ├── rc          → proposed: pre-release freeze point
│   ├── beta        → proposed: wider pre-release
│   ├── nightly     → proposed: cron of main
│   ├── edge        → proposed: per-push artifact
│   └── debug       → proposed: verbosity-only, never distributed
│
├── HOST         which Discord (or browser) it runs in (choose 1)
│   ├── discord-stable      ✅  TODAY
│   ├── discord-ptb         ✅  TODAY
│   ├── discord-canary      ✅  TODAY
│   ├── discord-development ✅  TODAY
│   ├── web                 ✅  TODAY (extension / userscript)
│   └── custom-client       → proposed: best-effort, unsupported
│
└── ROLLOUT      how the next TRACK build reaches you  (choose 1)
    ├── full            ✅  TODAY (hash-flip)
    ├── canary-rollout  → proposed: opt-in volunteer cohort
    ├── progressive     → proposed: 1% → 10% → 100% by telemetry
    ├── featureflagged  → proposed: disabled-by-default toggles
    └── rollback        → proposed: always-on capability, never "a channel"
```

And a maintenance ring a track can *enter*:

```plaintext
Production     testing     unstable     volatile     internal
   │              │            │            │            │
   ▼              ▼            ▼            ▼            ▼
 stable ◀──── beta ────── dev ─────── edge ─── debug
   │  ─ lts ───┘  └── rc ──┘   └ nightly ┘
   └ rollback / hotfix / security-patch / maintenance-release lanes
```

### Concrete recommendations for the Limey V1 updater

[Section titled “Concrete recommendations for the Limey V1 updater”](#concrete-recommendations-for-the-limey-v1-updater)

1. **Ship today’s reality under two IDs.** Keep `stable` and `dev` as the only two *selectable* tracks in the settings dropdown for the MVP, with `devbuild` as `dev`’s display alias. Everything above is additive.
2. **Model channels as data, not code.** A channel is an object — `{ id, displayName, description, audience, stability, cadence, origin, supportedHosts, artifacts, rollout }` — so the same spec powers the settings dropdown, the CLI (`--track dev --host discord-ptb`), and the changelog page.
3. **Never let rollout override track.** % cohorts and hotfix-priority apply within a track; they are not new tracks. This is what keeps “why am I not on the newest version?” support tickets answerable.
4. **Aliases, not duplicates.** `preview-ch`→`beta`, `insider`→`beta`, `snapshot`→`nightly`, `rolling`→`dev`, `security-patch`→`hotfix` (with a flag) — collapse the naming family onto one canonical artifact.
5. **Mark proposed names visually.** In the settings UI, render unimplemented channels as grayed-out with a “coming later” tooltip so users never believe a non-existent feed exists.

# Bot SDK

> Connect your Discord bot to Limey V1 — Limes economy, ban registry, plugin store and more

The official **Limey V1 Bot SDK** lets third-party Discord bots integrate with the Limey V1 platform. One import, no dependencies required, works with any bot stack (discord.js, oceanic.js, Eris, raw REST…).

```js
import { LimeyV1 } from "https://limey-discord.onrender.com/sdk/index.js";


const limey = new LimeyV1();
```

🍋 One import

Served straight from this site as a pure ES module. Node 18+, serverless, or any bundler that supports remote ESM. No npm package required.

🪙 Limes economy

Wallets, daily claims, message/voice/stream/game activity, perk tiers, trials and subscriptions — all computed server-side.

🚫 Ban registry

Check any Discord user against the official Limey V1 ban registry so you can keep trust-sensitive actions consistent with the platform.

🧩 Plugin store

List community plugins or look one up by name. Great for /plugins commands and inline embeds.

🔎 Invite lookups

Resolve invites and guild widgets without your own Discord REST token.

🏷 Release channels

Read the machine-readable release-channel manifest from `client.channels` — what ships today vs proposed labels.

🛡️ Sentinel

Complete the Limey Sentinel proof-of-work check in-process for gated flows.

## Quick start

[Section titled “Quick start”](#quick-start)

```js
// 1. Show the platform banner when your bot boots.
const banner = await limey.status.get();
if (banner.active) console.log("[limey]", banner.message);


// 2. Ban registry — check any user before trust-sensitive actions.
const banned = await limey.bans.isBanned("123456789012345678");


// 3. Community plugin listing on a /plugins command.
const plugins = await limey.plugins.list();
```

Self-hosting Limey? Point `baseUrl` at your own instance instead:

```js
const limey = new LimeyV1({ baseUrl: "http://localhost:3000" });
```

## Limes economy

[Section titled “Limes economy”](#limes-economy)

All rates, streaks, caps and cooldowns are enforced server-side — you just forward activity. Batch message activity instead of hitting it per-message: the server awards 1 Lime per 25 messages, capped per day.

```js
// Wallet overview (balance, streak, tier, multiplier, nextDailyAt):
const wallet = await limey.limes.wallet(userId);


// Daily claim (server 429s when too early — err.code === "rate_limited"):
const claim = await limey.limes.claimDaily(userId);
// claim = { amount, balance, streak, streakBonus, multiplier }


// Batch message activity from your gateway:
await limey.limes.countMessages(userId, 25);


// Voice / streaming / game minutes, awarded per 15-minute block:
await limey.limes.countVoice(userId, 15);
await limey.limes.countStreaming(userId, 15);
await limey.limes.countGame(userId, 15);


// Perk tiers: Seedling / Grove / Orchard
const { tiers } = await limey.limes.tiers();
await limey.limes.startTrial(userId, "seedling"); // once per tier, ever
await limey.limes.subscribe(userId, "orchard");   // costs Limes
```

## Error handling

[Section titled “Error handling”](#error-handling)

Every failure throws a `LimeyV1Error` with a stable `code`. Retries on 429/5xx are automatic; every request has a 15s timeout. Both are tunable on the client.

```js
import { LimeyV1, LimeyV1Error } from "https://limey-discord.onrender.com/sdk/index.js";


try {
    await limey.limes.claimDaily(userId);
} catch (err) {
    if (err instanceof LimeyV1Error && err.code === "rate_limited") {
        // cooldown — err.data.nextDailyAt tells you when
    }
}
```

| code                | meaning                                         |
| ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `network_error`     | fetch failed / timed out (status = 0)           |
| `rate_limited`      | HTTP 429 after retries                          |
| `server_error`      | HTTP 5xx after retries                          |
| `api_error`         | other non-2xx (`err.data` holds the body)       |
| `not_found`         | unknown plugin / bot-state key / lookup         |
| `sentinel_required` | 403 asking for a proof-of-work payload          |
| `invalid_id`        | malformed Discord snowflake passed by your code |

## Admin token + `bot-state`

[Section titled “Admin token + bot-state”](#admin-token--bot-state)

The **limebot** mirrors its SQLite feature tables into the server’s Postgres kv store so deploys don’t wipe counting progress. Bots that plug into the same ecosystem can do the same with `USRBG_ADMIN_TOKEN`:

```js
const limey = new LimeyV1({ adminToken: process.env.USRBG_ADMIN_TOKEN });
await limey.state.set("my-feature", { enabled: true, since: Date.now() });
const cfg = await limey.state.get("my-feature");
```

Keys are restricted to `[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}` (server-validated).
